scope_note: Two-pass direct-evidence audit plus directed third and adversarial fourth audits for Apple Prineville. The selected inventory object is one 9,228-square-foot IM3 building at approximately 44.2894155, -120.8750775, not Apple's full 1600 SW Baldwin Road campus, the two Business Oregon long-term-rural-zone facilities (DC No. 1 and DC No. 2), all 15 current Apple assessor matches, later 300,000-plus-square-foot expansions, supporting renewable projects, or Meta's separate campus. All retained campus, facility, company/county, single-account and supporting-infrastructure values therefore remain unallocated. Exact direct evidence now covers annual electricity, two investment and hiring forecasts, one reported campus jobs snapshot, annual potential additional tax, two exempt facility values, taxable company value and tax billed, ten annual payments for one 96.90-acre Apple land account, and an Apple SDC contribution. Permit valuations, construction workforce/payroll, supplier payments and geography, operating payroll/residence, community award values, all-account tax-payment reconciliation, project water consumption, same-scope service costs and causal county outcomes remain unavailable or fail the boundary test.

project_updates.title: Investment audit — two facility proposals retained without relabeling them as spend
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Business Oregon LTREZ structured data and attachments; City budgets, development agreements and planning packets; Apple releases; assessor values; permit records; contractor pages; SEC EDGAR. Retained: DC No. 1 proposed investment $250,000,000 at 2012-04-12 certification and DC No. 2 proposed investment $226,400,000 at 2016-02-25 certification, both campus/facility scope, unallocated, source projections. Boundaries: the required minima were $8.5 million and $200 million; proposed investment is not realized spend, assessed value, permit valuation or selected-building cost. Adversarial fourth pass repeated exact Apple Inc./Prineville/DC No. 1/DC No. 2 searches in Socrata resource re77-krua and all 2016-2025 attachments, City Ordinances 1195/1219 and Resolutions 1571/1573, the assessor's 15 Apple matches, ePermitting's 1600 Bal address inventory, and Apple EDGAR filings; none disclosed realized Prineville capex. Indispensable missing input: an audited facility/phase expenditure ledger with payment or placed-in-service dates and a crosswalk to IM3 building 00397914434.

project_updates.title: Construction audit — address inventory reviewed; no original-building valuation retained
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Oregon ePermitting Building; Crook County work-session/planning packets; City ordinances and budgets; Turner, Fortis, DPR, Southland, CriticalArc, Rosendin and NxGen references; OSHA and BOLI public pages. Anonymous ePermitting search used 01/01/2011-09/06/2026, street 1600, fragment Bal and city Prineville, producing 100+ records. Opened 217-26-000747-STR: Permit Issued, owner Apple, Turner Construction Company CCB 69988, 'Apple, IW ph2,' temporary 348-square-foot restroom job trailer. The fourth pass invoked Download results; the public UI queued one item under Reports (1) but exposed no accessible row-level export or original-building crosswalk. Boundaries: the opened permit is a 2026 phase-two temporary structure, not the selected 9,228-square-foot object or original 2012 build. Indispensable missing inputs: original permit/application IDs crosswalked to the selected object, nonoverlapping final valuations, start/end dates, worker-hours, payroll, worker residence and contractor/subcontractor split. No construction record retained.

project_updates.title: Supplier audit — contractor identities found without payment or geography evidence
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: ePermitting applicant/licensed-professional fields; Apple supplier-responsibility and jobs pages; Turner/Fortis/DPR/Rosendin/Southland/CriticalArc project pages; City/County procurement and council packets; Oregon CCB/BOLI portals. Turner is directly named on opened permit 217-26-000747-STR; other pages identify Prineville scopes for confidential or differently labeled campuses but do not establish Apple payment. The fourth pass repeated exact Apple/Prineville and 1600 SW Baldwin searches across those routes; contractor identity and CCB 69988 were the strongest result. Boundaries: identity or office location is not supplier spend, local ownership, worker residence or selected-building attribution. Indispensable missing inputs: invoices or contract-paid amounts, vendor and subcontractor addresses at payment time, scope/phase tags, a nonoverlap rule, and household-income inputs. No supplier record retained.

project_updates.title: Operations audit — one reported jobs snapshot separated from forecasts and requisitions
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: joint City/Apple release; Business Oregon LTREZ facility rows; Apple Prineville careers; Central Oregon Community College; City Economic Opportunities Analysis; Oregon Employment Department/QualityInfo and WorkSource; BOLI apprenticeship/OATS. Retained: 100 jobs reported created by the campus in the 2018-12-19 release; 35 and 10 required/expected hires for DC No. 1 and No. 2 as source projections. The fourth pass repeated exact Apple/Prineville employer and training-agent searches; it found current 40-hour vacancies and the City's approximately 700 combined Apple/Meta employees, neither an Apple realized headcount. Boundaries: the 100 has no FTE, direct/contractor, residence, payroll or exact observation definition. Indispensable missing inputs: dated site HR headcount/FTE, employer and contract payroll by occupation, worksite versus residence, contractor status, turnover and apprenticeship completion.

project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Apple environmental/community pages and local news; City/County packets; Crook County School District; Central Oregon Community College; NeighborImpact; Crook County Kids Club; first-responder references; local nonprofits and named recipients. COCC confirms one described third-party-contract placement could earn three CIS credits and faculty toured the Apple site; the 2018 City release says Apple provided iPads to first responders. Fourth-pass exact-domain searches for Apple Prineville donations/grants at Crook County schools, COCC, NeighborImpact and City check-register/payment routes returned unrelated grants or unattributed support, not an Apple award. Boundaries: academic credits are not jobs or funding, and equipment without quantity/value/date is not a monetary contribution. Indispensable missing input: recipient confirmation naming Apple, amount or quantity and fair value, payment/date, purpose, beneficiary geography and campus-versus-corporate attribution. No community record retained.

project_updates.title: Boundary and identity audit — one IM3 building separated from campus, facilities and accounts
project_updates.notes: IM3 selects one 9,228-square-foot building near 44.2894155, -120.8750775. Apple reports the Prineville data center renewable since opening May 2012; City/State planning material describes a 1600 SW Baldwin Road campus with three much larger buildings developed through 2023 and later expansions. On 2026-09-07 the Crook County portal was queried by Name=APPLE across pages 1-2: 15 Apple Inc. matches, 12 real and three personal, were distinguished from unrelated pineapple names. Real accounts span tax lots 15160700 00101/00102 and 15150000 00312. Account 19371 shows tax lot 151500-00-00312, enterprise-zone class and a 2012 industrial improvement but no payment rows. Fourth-pass account 19494 shows tax lot 151607-00-00102, 96.90 acres, no improvements and ten 2016-2025 payments. Business Oregon separately labels DC No. 1 and DC No. 2. No parcel, account, payment, DC facility or later phase is treated as the selected building.
project_updates.project_description: Apple's Prineville data-center project is an Apple-operated campus at 1600 SW Baldwin Road in Prineville, Crook County, Oregon; the selected IM3 object is one mapped 9,228-square-foot building, not the entire campus. Apple reports that the Prineville data center has used 100 percent renewable electricity since opening in May 2012, while public planning material describes three much larger campus buildings developed through 2023. Business Oregon separately labels two enterprise-zone facilities DC No. 1 and DC No. 2, and none of those campus or facility totals is allocated to the selected building.

project_updates.title: Adversarial fourth-pass disposition — one direct series added; every other gap tied to indispensable inputs
project_updates.notes: Direct addition: Crook account 19494/R supplied ten exact tax-year 2016-2025 payment rows, receipts 238920-444833, retained only at single-account/company-county scope. Investment still requires an audited Prineville facility/phase capex ledger and IM3 crosswalk. Construction requires original permit IDs, final nonoverlapping valuations, dates, worker-hours/payroll/residence and contractor tiers. Suppliers require paid invoices/contracts, vendor addresses and phase tags. Operations requires dated site direct/contract FTE, payroll, occupation and residence. Fiscal requires the other 14 Apple account histories, treasurer reconciliation/distribution and building mapping. Public costs require a complete PILOT/fee/incentive ledger and same-scope realized service costs. Resources require a building-meter crosswalk, demand/charge data, water bills and generator permit inventory. Community requires recipient-confirmed amount/quantity/value, date, purpose and attribution. County employment, wages and GDP require a dated Apple phase treatment series, a defensible exposure share and a comparison/counterfactual separating Meta and later Apple phases. Without these category-specific inputs, ratio, footprint, staffing, multiplier, before-after and break-even substitutes would create false precision; no modeled values were added.

project_updates.title: Modeling audit — every last-resort candidate rejected after direct-evidence review
project_updates.notes: Investment: rejected — direct facility forecasts exist, but no realized spend or selected-building allocation supports a truthful bound. Construction: rejected — no project worker count, duration, wage or original-building permit ledger. Suppliers: rejected — identities lack payments and geography. Operations: rejected — the 100-job snapshot lacks direct/contractor and residence definitions; continuous-coverage staffing would require unsupported post counts and shift assumptions. Fiscal: rejected — one land-account payment series now exists, but the remaining accounts, recipient distribution and selected-building allocation are absent; allocating any total to one footprint would be arbitrary. Public costs: rejected — a same-account break-even would merely restate unallocated tax while service costs, recipients and abatements use incompatible scopes. Resources: rejected — direct annual campus electricity already exists, while building allocation, water use and demand bounds lack defensible inputs. Community: rejected — no monetary recipient confirmation. County employment: rejected; County wages: rejected; County GDP: rejected — multiple Apple phases and Meta's separate campus defeat a credible treatment share and counterfactual. Modeled additions: zero; direct forecasts added: four.
